detailed_description:
The source video governs how the whole scene is photographed, including the replacement people. Render their appearance within that same source-shot lighting and image texture. Identity comes from the pictures; photographic rendering comes from <Video 1>.
Follow all existing shots, cuts, actions and interactions in <Video 1> over its exact 15-second timeline. Keep the five pairings separate through cuts and overlaps. A replacement appears only where its corresponding source performer is present; do not insert it elsewhere or replace an unselected bystander.
Preserve each source performer's continuous movement and visible mouth performance, not the still pose or expression in the photograph. Keep a listener listening when somebody else speaks. Replace the entire selected character, including head, hands, body and feet, consistently with its reference identity and clothing.
All selected performers share the same cyan overlay at 20% opacity. The color marks selection, not identity; use the defined position/time anchors for identity. Face-mesh lines describe facial motion only. Remove all cyan and mesh marks from the finished footage.
overall_soundscape: Reuse the original dialogue, ambience, laughter and effects from <Audio 1>, retaining their source timing and speaker associations.
non_diegetic_music: Retain only music already present in <Audio 1>; add none.
visual_findings: All five replacement references remain recognizable in the seven sampled source-shot intervals.
The unselected background person in shot 5 is retained here, unlike the recent unchanged control repeat.
Opening changes to a wider over-the-shoulder composition rather than retaining source framing.
Dario holds the reference photograph's raised pinched-hand pose through samples at 6.2, 6.7, 7.2 and 7.7 seconds, while the source performer's hands are down.
Sam remains front-facing and portrait-like at 11.0 and 11.5 seconds; no clear consistent scene-texture advantage is established.
The final wide shot is already visible at 12.0 seconds, earlier than the source cut at approximately 12.708 seconds.
